text: Three seconds left, and the hill sits up: a shell of mossy slate plates, and under it, a calm grey giant.
Answered. And the call holds while the called one speaks.
The giant leans toward the rift and takes his time. Hello.
Jaeha, chest-deep and sweating: hello, nice to meet you, they have three seconds.
He's slow on purpose, the giant says. Slow things arrive. What can the Operator offer?
Behind him, his mossy field runs to a little hut, and a black tide creeps toward it.
No pitch now. He can't promise a garden; he lives on a roof in Seoul. But he can promise a roof, and he'll carry what hits him.
The giant's slow eyes widen. Nobody has ever offered to carry anything for him.
A huge hand reaches out, gentle as if lifting an egg, and the black hand on Jaeha's ankle lets go. A roof, then.
Accepted. Summon number two is coming through.
In the room, a slit tears open over the bed, and Nib shoves Jaeha to the floor.
The giant drops through onto the bed, which folds flat. His shell scrapes the ceiling. Seoa screams.
He bows: he is Borro, and he broke their bed. Next time, Nib says, he goes through doors first.
Sunday morning. Borro, stoneback carrier of the Far Side, summon number two, with a shield the size of a door.
Seal one of five, five minutes of field form, both summon slots full. And Route Alignment drops from a hundred to zero.
His new home: a blue tarp over a flattened mattress. He was promised a roof. He's on a roof.
Borro thinks about it very slowly. Technically.
He plants one seed in a styrofoam fish box, gently, as if it might break.
Then Nib spots Jaeha's ankle. Something touched him over there. It let go when Borro took his hand.
A bruise shaped like long fingers with too many joints.
The landlady stares up and up. What is that? A husk, says Seoa. A big one. Not a pet.
Seoa will buy rice cakes at the market Tuesday after school, for his welcome dinner. He likes rice cakes. Probably.
Tuesday's job pays two million cash, no streaming. Good. The big one isn't ready for the internet.
D-grade Gate 4402, seventh floor of an unfinished tower in Mapo. Borro wears a white husk face tied on with cord.
The site manager stares up. Biggest husk he's ever seen. Is it equipment?
Borro's masked head turns slowly. He is not equipment. Ventriloquism, sir. Still a hobby.
Inside, the floor is a ruin open to an orange sky, slabs cracking away either side of one long solid beam.
Under Borro's feet, the concrete cracks.
Nib: he's too heavy for this floor. Borro: he's the right weight; the floor is too thin.
Then lean black shapes slink out between the columns. Eight of them.
Ash hounds: eyeless, wolf-sized, all bone teeth, and an alpha twice their size.
The alpha howls, and every hound's head snaps toward them at once.
Jaeha's notes: they only move when the big one howls. Cut the howl, the pack breaks.
The slabs won't hold Borro. The beam will. And the edges are still attached.
Borro, stand on the beam and let nothing past. Nib, go round the edge and cut the big one's throat.
Jaeha links to both, Nib's view on one side, Borro's on the other.
Borro plants himself on the beam, shield up like a door, and the pack charges along it.
Three smash into the iron. Borro slides back half a step, and a hound flies off into the dark.
Jaeha's heels grind back with him: Carry puts thirty percent of Borro's hit in his body.
Nib runs a rim of concrete no wider than a foot, seven storeys of air beside him.
It breaks under him. He catches a coil of rebar one-handed.
On the beam, one hound leaps clean over the shield at Borro's head.
Jaeha throws out both hands: field form for both, five minutes each, and he shares the load of two.
Borro heaves the shield forward and hurls the whole pack back down the beam.
But the hound hanging from his shield rakes his arm, and the gash opens on Jaeha's shoulder. Load: a hundred and ten percent.
Yerin presses on the wound. He's taking both their hits! That's the deal he made.
Nib swings round the far column and drops right behind the alpha.
It throws its head back to howl again.
His knives cross its throat in an X, and the howl dies.
With no howl to follow, the pack spins in circles. Borro stamps on the slab beside the beam.
The slab drops away, carrying the hounds into the dark. Borro stands alone on the beam.
The dying alpha lunges once more, and Nib drives both knives into its neck. Ash.
Then, quiet. The glow fades from both summons.
Jaeha slides down the wall, bleeding, shaking. Carry load a hundred and forty percent. Overload warning.
Borro kneels to his level. The claw hit Borro's arm, but Jaeha's shoulder is bleeding. He carries what hits him.
Boss defeated: Ash Hound Alpha, D-grade. A new kind of boss, and Route Alignment climbs to forty.
Again, only harvest. Jaeha writes it down. That's twice.
At dusk they limp out, and the site manager hands over the envelope without looking at Borro.
Then every phone on the street shrieks at once.
Emergency alert. Dungeon break at Mangwon Market. Monsters in the streets. Evacuate now.
Jaeha's pupils shrink. Tuesday. She said Tuesday, after school. Rice cakes.
Seoa at the stair door, smiling back as she made that promise.
A kilometre away, black smoke rises over Mangwon, lit red from below.
His phone rings. Seoa.
Seoa, where is she? At the market, she says. And she needs him to listen very carefully.
